HI-2026-GM1370.title: Informing the Legislature that on July 16, 2026, the following bill became law without the Governor's signature: SB847 SD2 HD2 CD1 (Act 266).

actions.text: Received.

HI-2026-GM1370.aiSummary: The measure became law on July 16, 2026, as Act 266. It creates a three-year pilot program in Kauai and Hawaii counties that would let certain licensed clinical psychologists, under a doctor or psychiatrist’s supervision, prescribe some mental health medicines to patients ages 18 to 65 at federally qualified health centers. The state health planning and development agency would report back to lawmakers on whether to expand, make permanent, or end the program.

HI-2026-SB2851.title: RELATING TO DEAF INDIVIDUALS.
HI-2026-SB2851.summary: Authorizes deaf motor vehicle owners to register their vehicle as being owned by a deaf individual so that a deafness designation appears when a law enforcement officer accesses the motor vehicle's information. Effective 1/1/2027. (CD1)

HI-2026-SB2338.title: RELATING TO HOUSING.
HI-2026-SB2338.summary: Exempts Hawaii Housing Finance and Development Corporation employees from the requirement that their employment actions and job descriptions be subject to approval by the Director of Business, Economic Development, and Tourism. Requires the Executive Director of HHFDC to be paid a salary recommended by its Board of Directors and subject to the approval of the Director of Business, Economic Development, and Tourism, not to exceed ninety-nine per cent of the salary of the Governor. Renames the position of Executive Assistant to Deputy Executive Director for HHFDC and increases the salary cap for the Deputy Executive Director. Establishes conditions for the issuance, renewal, and termination of employment contracts issued by the HHFDC, Hawaii Community Development Authority, and the Hawaii Public Housing Authority. Exempts the Executive Director of HCDA, and officers, agents, and employees appointed by the Executive Director, from the requirement that their employment actions and job descriptions be subject to approval by the Director of Business, Economic Development, and Tourism. Requires the Executive Director of HCDA to be paid a salary recommended by the Authority and subject to the approval of the Director of Business, Economic Development, and Tourism, not to exceed ninety-nine per cent of the salary of the Governor. (CD1)

HI-2026-SB2338.aiSummary: The law changes hiring and pay rules for staff at the Hawaii Housing Finance and Development Corporation, the Hawaii Community Development Authority, and the Hawaii Public Housing Authority. It removes some approval steps for certain employees, sets rules for employment contracts, and changes some job titles and salary limits. It also sets pay rules for the executive directors of HHFDC and HCDA, with their salaries capped at no more than 99% of the governor’s salary.

HI-2026-GM1361.title: Informing the Legislature that on July 15, 2026, the Governor signed the following bill into law: SB2999 SD1 HD2 CD1 (ACT 258).

actions.text: Received.

HI-2026-GM1361.aiSummary: The bill became Act 258 and requires the Department of Transportation to set rules for a clean fuel standard in Hawaii by January 1, 2028. The rules must phase in lower carbon fuel standards, with diesel and gasoline starting on January 1, 2029, and use a method for measuring greenhouse gas emissions across a fuel’s full life cycle. It affects fuel producers and users in the state, and the standards are meant to cut emissions from transportation fuels.

HI-2026-SB3001.title: RELATING TO ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE.
HI-2026-SB3001.summary: Requires operators of AI companions in the State to issue certain disclosures to users. Requires operators to develop certain protocols to respond to user prompts regarding suicidal ideation or self-harm. Establishes protections for users and minor users of AI companions. Beginning 1/1/2028, requires operators to submit annual reports to the Behavioral Health Administration of the Department of Health containing certain information. Establishes that violations are to be considered unfair or deceptive acts or practices. (CD1)

HI-2026-SB3001.aiSummary: Requires people who run AI companions in Hawaii to give users certain notices and to set up steps for prompts about suicidal thoughts or self-harm. It also adds protections for users, including minors, and starts yearly reports to the Health Department on 1/1/2028. Breaking these rules can be treated as an unfair or deceptive business practice.

HI-2026-HB1785.title: RELATING TO STUDENT TRANSPORTATION.
HI-2026-HB1785.summary: Authorizes the Superintendent to hire a new contractor if a contractor under a student transportation contract fails to provide service on a contracted service capacity or designated service segment for five or more consecutive instructional days. Authorizes the Department of Education to assess a penalty if a contractor fails to provide service on a designated service segment without an approved justification. Authorizes the use of the School Bus Fare Revolving Fund to offset costs associated with procuring replacement services. (CD1)

HI-2026-HB1785.aiSummary: The law lets the Superintendent hire a new contractor if a student bus contractor misses service for five or more straight school days. It also lets the Department of Education charge a penalty when a contractor misses a service segment without an approved reason. The School Bus Fare Revolving Fund may be used to help pay for replacement service.

HI-2026-GM1349.aiSummary: Signed into law on July 14, 2026, this act sets rules for AI-made fake images, audio, or video that look like a real person. It makes it unlawful to publish a realistic digital imitation of an identifiable person without consent if it is used in ads, causes harm, or is used for fraud, defamation, harassment, or other crimes. It also gives people a way to seek civil remedies, and it does not apply to parody, satire, commentary, criticism, scholarship, political or educational expression, news reporting, or some documentary or historical uses.

HI-2026-GM1343.aiSummary: The law changes Hawaii’s school impact fee rules for housing projects. It expands exemptions for certain homes, including projects with fewer than 500 units, some affordable units, and small studio units, and it sets new timing rules for land dedication or fee-in-lieu agreements for projects with 100 or more units. It also repeals a sunset and reporting rule, restructures some school fee accounts, and keeps existing education contribution agreements in place.

HI-2026-GM1334.aiSummary: The governor signed this measure into law as Act 232 on July 10, 2026. It deals with state bonds and includes findings about Hawaii’s debt limit. The act lists past and estimated net general fund revenue and bond debt figures used to check that limit.

HI-2026-GM1325.title: Informing the Legislature that on July 9, 2026, the Governor signed the following bill into law: HB1974 HD1 SD1 CD1 (ACT 223).

actions.text: Received.

HI-2026-GM1325.aiSummary: Signed into law on July 9, 2026, this measure requires the state health planning and development agency to make a state plan on hearing loss. The plan must review hearing loss data, screening, access to care, training, and ways to improve services and awareness. It also sets a first report due before the 2027 regular session and provides $100,000 for fiscal year 2026-2027 to help develop and publish the plan.
